liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Foolish Heart** (3 reviews): Reviewer calls this Foolish Heart the worst ever, with Jerry singing around the right key; Defends Foolish Heart: not tight, but Jerry gave it everything despite his worn voice [8][10][11]
- **Playing In The Band** (2 reviews): Seventeen-minute Playin' is the highlight, evoking the early 1970s; Seventeen-minute Playin' is named the highlight [9][18]
- **Throwing Stones** (2 reviews): The Throwing Stones jam still moves this reviewer, possibly because of the percussion; Attendee's best memories are the Foolish Heart and the Throwing Stones jam [14][17]
- **Shakedown Street** (1 review): Opening Shakedown ran about eleven minutes and was snaky [8]
- **Big River** (1 review): Big River and Maggie's Farm opened as a cowboy-song pairing, which the reviewer enjoyed [9]
- **I Want to Tell You** (1 review): Psychedelic I Want to Tell You was one of two Beatles covers; reviewer loved it [13]
- Jerry forgot some lyrics, which reviewer says detracts from the show [15]

## Setlist highlights

- **I Want to Tell You**: rare: 7 archived performances [20]

## The recordings

- **gd94-07-19.sbd.carr.8476.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 18 songs; 162 min; rated 3.87/5 by 23 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the recording has great sound; Reviewer finds the sound decent, though used to second-generation audience tapes [13][14]
- **gd1994-07-19.nak300.bleich.GEMS.92433.flac16**: source not stated; 18 songs; 163 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [3]. Said about its sound: Nice, solid recording with good detail and full sound [3]
- **gd1994-07-19.sbd.carr.tetzeli.fix-8476.35164.reflac.flac16**: soundboard; 18 songs; 162 min; rated 3/5 by 4 [2]
- **gd1994-07-19.nak300.holtz.jaz.91836.flac16**: source not stated; 18 songs; 168 min [4]

## Around the show

- It rained off and on during most of the show, making the Rain encore fitting [9]
- Reviewer attended this as their first concert, at age 15 [13]
- Attendee first heard the show again twelve years later, after finding the site [17]
- Sixteen-year-old attendee drove from Michigan with sister and friends in their dad's van; had just seen Pink Floyd in Detroit [19]
- Reviewer says the following two nights of the Deer Creek run were much better than this one [8]
- Says Deer Creek was great until newer fans stormed the fences the following year [10]
- Reviewer says the show could not compare to Pink Floyd's 1994 tour show at the Silverdome [19]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd94-07-19.sbd.carr.8476.sbeok.shnf**: source: DSBd>?>CDR [1]. Also: Digital soundboard source, via unknown steps to CDR, seeded to etree by Dan Carr [1]
- **gd1994-07-19.nak300.bleich.GEMS.92433.flac16**: taped by John Bleich; transferred by BGreen; source: Nak 300's > D6 [3]
- **gd1994-07-19.sbd.carr.tetzeli.fix-8476.35164.reflac.flac16**: transferred by Dan Carr and Bill Tetzeli; source: DSBD>?>CDR>EAC>WAV>SHNv3>WAV>FLAC [2]
- **gd1994-07-19.nak300.holtz.jaz.91836.flac16**: taped by Greg Holtz; transferred by JAZ; source: Nakamichi Cm300's with Cp-4 guns/PZM 30D's mix-> D3 DAT [4]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Michael Mullen Grateful Dead: [1994-07-20 Deer Creek Music Center, Noblesville, IN, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1994-07-20-deer-creek-music-center-noblesville-in-usa/) [21]
